label: Tabletop Games
blurb: Games played on a table with objects you own, and usually painted yourself, in front of people who are in the room.

nodes.label: Warhammer
nodes.blurb: Assemble it, paint it, then lose with it. Two thirds of the hobby happens at a desk on your own before anything happens on a table.

nodes.label: Tabletop RPGs
nodes.blurb: Four people, some dice and a shared story that only exists while everyone is at the table. The cheapest entry on this whole map.

nodes.label: Skirmish Games
nodes.blurb: Ten models instead of a hundred. The format that lets someone finish a force, which is the format most people should start with.

nodes.label: Terrain Building
nodes.blurb: Foam, card and sprue offcuts turned into ruins to fight over. A table of painted armies on bare board still looks unfinished.

nodes.label: Historical Wargaming
nodes.blurb: Real battles at scale, with rules arguing about frontage and morale. Where the research is half the pleasure.

nodes.label: List Building
nodes.blurb: Building a force inside a points budget. A puzzle you can play for an hour without opening a box.

nodes.label: Tournaments
nodes.blurb: Five games in a weekend against strangers. The deadline that finally gets an army painted.

nodes.label: Setting and Lore
nodes.blurb: The novels, the codices and forty years of accumulated background. Plenty of people are only here for this.

nodes.label: Running a Game
nodes.blurb: Preparation, pacing and improvising when the players do the thing you did not write. A performance skill wearing a hobby's coat.

nodes.label: Game Design
nodes.blurb: Writing rules that survive contact with people trying to win. Playtesting is where the design actually happens.

nodes.label: Print and Play
nodes.blurb: A PDF, a printer and an evening with a craft knife. How most designs get tested before anyone spends money.

nodes.label: Dice and Accessories
nodes.blurb: Sets, trays, towers and the sharp-edged resin ones. A small collecting hobby attached to every game in this cluster.

nodes.label: Card Games
nodes.blurb: Constructed decks, draft nights and a secondary market that behaves like a small stock exchange.

nodes.label: Board Games
nodes.blurb: Everything from forty minutes to a full Saturday. The gateway most of this cluster arrives through.

nodes.label: Solo Play
nodes.blurb: Games designed for one, and campaigns played against a deck instead of an opponent. What the hobby does when nobody is free.

edges.note: Ten models, one box, finished. The version of this hobby people actually complete.
